solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Become confused by puzzle’s first row (6)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of 'puzzle'
places the two pieces side by side

blocks.note: to addle is to become muddled

annotation.surface: A solver gets in a muddle over the top line of the grid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line of squares in the grid, and 'puzzle' like the crossword itself; row is the verb, what you do with an oar.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean propelling a small boat with oars or a blade, and the surface hides it as a line of grid squares.

entries.clue: Taken in by one patient’s deception (3-2,3)

blocks.note: a guest who is put up is taken in for the night
Job of the Bible, proverbial for his patience

annotation.surface: A trusting person is fooled by a patient in hospital faking illness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Patient' reads as someone in a hospital bed; here it is the adjective behind 'the patience of Job'.
annotation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a scheme rigged in advance to deceive.

entries.clue: Food evenly rolled, cooked in hollow leaves (8)

definitions.text: Food evenly rolled, cooked in hollow leaves

indicators.note: keeps the even-numbered letters of 'Food'
turns those letters round
puts MADE inside the next piece
empties 'leaves' to its outer letters

blocks.note: cooked = made, as a meal is made; it sits inside L…S

annotation.surface: A recipe: something rolled up and cooked inside leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the dish, since dolmades are fillings rolled and cooked in vine leaves.
annotation.definitionFit: Dolmades are a Greek dish of stuffed vine leaves, rolled and cooked.

entries.clue: Revolutionary material, regularly reordered (5)

indicators.note: rearranges the letters of 'material'

annotation.surface: Cloth rearranged on some fixed routine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' has to become a specific fabric before anything can be rearranged; only two letters of LINEN swap places.
annotation.definitionFit: Lenin led the Russian Revolution of 1917.

entries.clue: Getting in gin ordered by directors (8)

indicators.note: 'ordered' means put in a set order, so GIN's letters are arranged afresh
sets the pieces next to each other

blocks.note: a company's directors form its board

annotation.surface: The company directors order in some gin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Getting in' sounds like buying supplies, as in getting in the gin; it means climbing aboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both nouns for the act of climbing aboard a train, ship or plane.

entries.clue: Ill-equipped to make cocktails blue (3,2,7)

blocks.note: a bar with no spirits left can't mix drinks

annotation.surface: A bartender who can't make cocktails feels down about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Spirits are both strong drink and mood, so the one phrase covers an empty bar and a low mood.
annotation.definitionFit: With no spirits you cannot mix cocktails; out of spirits also means dejected.

entries.clue: On end of film make time for an artist (9)

indicators.note: takes the last letter of 'film'

blocks.note: a make of car is a brand

annotation.surface: At the end of the shoot, a director finds time for a painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Make' reads as a verb but is the noun, a make or brand of product.
annotation.definitionFit: Rembrandt was the great seventeenth-century Dutch painter.

entries.clue: Prompt noticeable when overheard (6)

indicators.note: says the answer sounds like a phrase for 'noticeable'

blocks.note: what is in sight can be noticed

annotation.surface: A cue from the prompter that the audience can hear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' suggests a theatre prompter being overheard; it is the verb, to urge on.
annotation.definitionFit: To incite someone is to prompt or urge them to act.

entries.clue: Soldiers’ ways of operating gadgets (6)

blocks.note: MO = modus operandi, a way of operating

annotation.surface: How soldiers go about their business.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe looks possessive but just pluralises the GIs; MO is short for the Latin modus operandi.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: informal words for clever little devices, gismo being a variant spelling of gizmo.

entries.clue: Books on fabrication expertise (6)

indicators.note: puts the books after the fabrication

blocks.note: a tale is a made-up story
NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: Books about skill in making things.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fabrication' suggests manufacturing, but it is a lie or story.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an aptitude or skill someone has, though talent leans to the innate where expertise is learned.

entries.clue: Stands for food processors (8)

blocks.note: the organs that digest what we eat, not kitchen gadgets

annotation.surface: Kitchen display units for food processors.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stands' looks like kitchen furniture and 'food processors' like appliances; one is the verb tolerates, the other the organs of digestion.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who stomachs something stands it; stomachs also process food.

entries.clue: Sad Scot no ladies fancy (12)

indicators.note: 'fancy' as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up into a new pattern

annotation.surface: A Scotsman is unhappy that no women take a shine to him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as a verb, to be attracted to; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means sad beyond comfort.

entries.clue: Patent dispute one challenges in court (9)

blocks.note: a tiff is a small quarrel

annotation.surface: An argument over a patent ends up before a judge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Patent' points to intellectual property; it is the adjective meaning obvious.
annotation.definitionFit: A plaintiff brings a case against someone in court.

entries.clue: Port drinking at five to six? (5)

indicators.note: the port takes AT inside it

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian port

annotation.surface: Having a glass of port just before six o'clock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Five to six' reads as a time, the drinking hour; it is a ratio, 5:6, and the question mark flags it as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 5:6, read 'five to six', is one proportion between two numbers.

entries.clue: Being of limited skill, I take in £25 (3-5,4)

blocks.note: to take someone in is to trick them
a pony is British slang for £25

annotation.surface: Someone of modest ability admits to earning just twenty-five pounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as a participle, but it is a noun, a creature; a pony is British slang for £25.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom, from a circus pony that can do only one trick, for a person or thing with a single talent.

entries.clue: Former African island in a novel (9)

indicators.note: new, rearranged: IN A becomes IAN

annotation.surface: An African character who once lived on an island in a book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book but is the adjective new, so IN A gets rearranged. Rhodesia is the former name of Zimbabwe.
annotation.definitionFit: A Rhodesian was a citizen of Rhodesia, a country that no longer exists under that name.

entries.clue: Cool attitude for example (8)

blocks.note: a stance is a position or attitude

annotation.surface: A laid-back manner, to give one example.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For example' looks like a stock phrase; it splits into the link 'for' and the definition 'example'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a single case cited to illustrate something, as in 'for instance'.

entries.clue: Artisan’s plastic rulers (8)

indicators.note: mouldable, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters, the 's supplying the S

annotation.surface: A craftsman's rulers made of plastic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rulers' look like measuring sticks in a workshop; they are empresses.
annotation.definitionFit: Tsarinas were Russian empresses, female rulers.

entries.clue: Trap gutless spies outside air bases (12)

indicators.note: removes the insides of 'spies'
puts S…S around the next piece

blocks.note: to corner someone is to trap them
an air or manner is a tone

annotation.surface: Cowardly spies are caught outside military air bases.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Air bases' looks like one phrase for an airfield; 'air' goes into the wordplay and 'bases' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Cornerstones are foundations, the bases something is built on.

entries.clue: Puzzle trainee’s kit (3,3)

blocks.note: a cub reporter is a trainee

annotation.surface: A new recruit is baffled by the equipment handed out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kit' looks like equipment; it is a young fox.
annotation.definitionFit: A specialist sense: kit is the proper name for the young of a fox, as it is for a ferret or beaver.

entries.clue: Start off at sea, perhaps unwell (6)

indicators.note: the start is taken off, so the word loses its first letter
being at sea is one example of sailing

blocks.note: sailing is one way of being at sea

annotation.surface: Setting off on a voyage and maybe feeling seasick.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start off' reads as setting out on the voyage; it is the instruction to remove the start.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adjectives describe someone in poor health.

entries.clue: Volunteer work leads to it never ending (5)

indicators.note: takes the first letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: the first letters of IT, NEVER, ENDING

annotation.surface: Charity work turns out to be endless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Volunteer' suggests an unpaid helper; it is the verb, to offer a view.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: both verbs mean offering a view unasked, as in 'she volunteered that it would rain'.

entries.clue: Who makes dresses abroad more attractive? (9)

blocks.note: fit is British slang for attractive

annotation.surface: A question about who makes foreign women look better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dresses' reads as a noun, frocks; it is the verb, to clothe. Fit is British slang for good-looking.
annotation.definitionFit: An outfitter supplies clothes, dressing people.

entries.clue: Race one part of the 24 hours at Le Mans (5)

blocks.clueFragment: part of the 24 hours at Le Mans

annotation.surface: One stretch of the famous Le Mans 24-hour motor race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Race' and Le Mans point to motor racing; the race is a people, and Le Mans only says the word is French.
annotation.definitionFit: Race in its older sense of a people sharing descent: here the Arctic peoples of Canada, Greenland and Alaska.

entries.clue: Urgent knocking (8)

annotation.surface: Someone hammering at the door in a hurry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocking' sounds like rapping on a door; it is disparaging, as in knocking someone's work.
annotation.definitionFit: Critical means both urgent and fault-finding.

entries.clue: Retire from November in an Italian city (4,2)

indicators.note: puts N inside the city's name

blocks.note: N is November in the radio alphabet

annotation.surface: Retiring from work in November to live in Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Retire from' reads as leaving a job; retire here means go to bed.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: in the sense of going to bed for the night, not leaving work.

entries.clue: Good pub embraced by ale novice (8)

indicators.note: puts G and INN inside BEER

annotation.surface: A decent pub run by a newcomer to real ale.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a pub and its ale, with the novice as a drinker; all three are pieces of the answer's letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone new to an activity and still learning it, which in the surface is the ale drinker.

entries.clue: Cattle drives (6)

blocks.note: castrated young bulls raised for beef
to steer a car is to drive it

annotation.surface: Herds of cattle being driven across the range.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cattle drives' reads as one noun phrase from a Western; split it into two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Steers are castrated bulls; steers also means drives or guides.
